summary: Today brought several production chains closer to completion. I finished setting up the lead plate furnace stack along with tin mining and smelting. The core materials for solder are now fully established — only the final production step remains.
To address the growing issue of byproducts, I implemented slaked lime evaporation. This converts the excess into lime and gravel, both of which are now fed directly into existing belts with priority.

I also made several optimizations across the base. Instead of converting all creosote into aromatics, I shifted production toward treated wood, only allowing overflow creosote to be processed further. This reduces unnecessary strain while making better use of available materials.

Fuel management required further adjustment. With the starter coal supply continuing to decline, I connected kerogen output from stone mining into steam production. It’s not a permanent solution, but it should help stabilize steam production in the short term.

The factory is beginning to feel more balanced — not because demand has decreased, but because waste is being redirected and systems are being tuned instead of expanded blindly. The next step is clear: bring solder production fully online.

Research saw solid progress today. I completed Basic Inventory Size 5, Basic Movement Speed 5, and Evaporation Processing 1 — the latter being critical for handling slaked lime and stabilizing the acetylene chain.

status.power: Stable; fuel diversification helping maintain consistent steam production.
status.production: All inputs ready for solder; treated wood prioritized over aromatics; byproduct handling stabilized.
status.science: Basic Inventory Size 5, Basic Movement Speed 5, and Evaporation Processing 1 completed.
status.defense: No significant incidents; base holding steady during internal restructuring.
